review_comments.body:
☑️ **Accepted as intended** — explained by @GauravChopada

---

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Void invoices export a full amount_due.** The `amount_due` column is `total_cents - amount_paid_cents` for every status, so a void invoice is exported as fully due. Voiding requires `amount_paid_cents` of 0, so a voided 1,500.00 invoice shows `amount_due` 1500.00. The export includes void rows by default, so an accountant summing that column overstates receivables. Voided invoices should export 0.00.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 6. The line number is from commit a29ef76; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Void invoices export a full amount_due — src/routes/exports.ts:74
The `amount_due` column is `total_cents - amount_paid_cents` for every status, so a void invoice is exported as fully due. Voiding requires `amount_paid_cents` of 0, so a voided 1,500.00 invoice shows `amount_due` 1500.00. The export includes void rows by default, so an accountant summing that column overstates receivables. Voided invoices should export 0.00.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🟡 **Test gap** | Minor

**Shadowing test cannot fail.** The 'export route does not shadow invoice lookups' test requests `GET /invoices/:id` for a real invoice, which succeeds whether or not `/invoices/export.csv` is registered. It checks the wrong direction. Shadowing would break `export.csv` itself (it would be read as an id and return 404), and the earlier export tests already cover that. Delete it, or assert `GET /invoices/export.csv` returns CSV, not a `not_found` JSON error.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 6. The line number is from commit a29ef76; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Minor · missing test] Shadowing test cannot fail — test/exports.test.ts:82
The 'export route does not shadow invoice lookups' test requests `GET /invoices/:id` for a real invoice, which succeeds whether or not `/invoices/export.csv` is registered. It checks the wrong direction. Shadowing would break `export.csv` itself (it would be read as an id and return 404), and the earlier export tests already cover that. Delete it, or assert `GET /invoices/export.csv` returns CSV, not a `not_found` JSON error.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🟡 **Test gap** | Minor

**Email formula neutralisation untested.** The export applies `plainText` to `customer_email` as well as `customer_name`. The route-level injection test only uses a malicious name, so removing `plainText` from the email column would leave the suite green. Create a second customer with an email such as `+cmd@example.com` or `=1+1@x.test` and assert the exported cell starts with an apostrophe.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 6. The line number is from commit a29ef76; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Minor · missing test] Email formula neutralisation untested — test/exports.test.ts:58
The export applies `plainText` to `customer_email` as well as `customer_name`. The route-level injection test only uses a malicious name, so removing `plainText` from the email column would leave the suite green. Create a second customer with an email such as `+cmd@example.com` or `=1+1@x.test` and assert the exported cell starts with an apostrophe.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>
This is intended. Accountants asked to see the original amount due on void invoices so they know what was cancelled.

Fair enough — if accountants specifically want to see the original amount cancelled on void invoices, exporting total_cents - amount_paid_cents (= total_cents, since voiding requires zero paid) makes sense as intended behavior. Accepted.
